blocked_reasons: findings are recorded without modifying the audited contracts
all output remains diagnostic-only and zero-credit

findings.evidence: A receipt can self-hash arbitrary command/booleans/PID; the production capability receipt has no manifest or checkpoint binding and no sealed process witness. The current capability is uninstalled, so no credit is currently promoted.
findings.hardening: Require the complete expected argv/cwd/environment plus manifest/training/checkpoint identity, and keep declarations non-authorizing without an in-memory real-Popen witness.
findings.risk: A future capability enablement could accept a successful-looking receipt for a different evaluator or source checkpoint.
findings.title: process proof and command/source identity are self-declared

findings.evidence: The code hashes or bounds a path and later opens that pathname again; a final stat/second digest cannot prevent a swap during the intervening HDF5/JSON read.
findings.hardening: Walk directory descriptors with O_NOFOLLOW, read the bytes once, and open HDF5 only from that bound byte snapshot.
findings.risk: A symlink or parent-directory race can make the validator read a different or out-of-bound artifact while retaining a passing pre/post pathname check.
findings.title: path TOCTOU before HDF5/artifact re-open

findings.evidence: The module-level _TERMINAL_CAPABILITY_TOKEN is import-accessible, execute_plan accepts it, and _run_popen_wait accepts an injected popen_factory while checking only isinstance(process, subprocess.Popen).
findings.hardening: Do not expose an executable token in a diagnostic module; reject execute requests at this boundary and require an independently sealed runtime witness before any future integration.
findings.risk: A same-process caller can bypass the stated unadmitted boundary or supply a subclass/fake process path if the token is used.
findings.title: residual terminal token and injectable Popen are not a sealed capability

findings.evidence: Required datasets are obtained with handle[name] without checking getlink(..., getlink=True) or Dataset.is_virtual.
findings.hardening: Reject every non-HardLink and every virtual dataset before dereference; inspect only the immutable in-memory snapshot.
findings.risk: A crafted HDF5 can dereference an external/soft/VDS source outside the checked artifact path.
findings.title: HDF5 external/soft links and virtual datasets are not rejected

findings.evidence: Evaluation and validator payloads validate selected fields but do not reject all unknown fields, unlike the outer receipt/process/artifact objects.
findings.hardening: Use an explicit versioned allowlist for each payload or preserve unknown fields only under an inert diagnostic namespace.
findings.risk: Future consumers can accidentally interpret an ignored field as an additional proof or completion signal.
findings.title: unknown-field handling is inconsistent at the production payload boundary
